sections.heading: Evolution & historical background of the Constitution

blocks.text: The Indian Constitution evolved from a **series of British colonial Acts (1773–1947)** and the **Constituent Assembly (1946–49)**. It draws on this legislative inheritance and world constitutions, and was **adopted on 26 Nov 1949** and **enforced on 26 Jan 1950**.

rows: First steps of Crown control over the Company.
Crown rule; **Indians in legislatures; separate electorates (1909)**.
**Dyarchy (1919); provincial autonomy, federation (1935)** — the biggest source of the Constitution.
Formed under the **Cabinet Mission Plan**; **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** President; **Ambedkar** chaired Drafting Committee; took **2 yrs 11 mo 18 days**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: making of the Constitution

items: **Constituent Assembly**: constituted under the **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)**; first met **9 Dec 1946** (Sachchidananda Sinha, temporary chair); **Dr Rajendra Prasad** = permanent President; **B.R. Ambedkar** = Chairman, **Drafting Committee** (7 members); **B.N. Rau** = constitutional advisor.

**Objectives Resolution** moved by **Nehru** (13 Dec 1946) → became the **Preamble**; adopted **26 Nov 1949** ('Constitution Day'); came into force **26 Jan 1950** (chosen — anniversary of Purna Swaraj 1930); took **2 yrs 11 months 18 days**.

**Borrowed features**: **British** (parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, CAG); **US** (Fundamental Rights, judicial review, preamble, VP); **Irish** (DPSP); **Canadian** (strong centre, residuary powers); **Australian** (concurrent list); **German (Weimar)** (emergency); **USSR** (Fundamental Duties, planning); **South African** (amendment procedure, RS election); **Japan** (procedure established by law).
**Historical acts leading up**: Regulating Act 1773, Charter Acts, **GoI Acts 1858/1919 (dyarchy)/1935 (main skeleton — federal scheme)**, Indian Independence Act 1947.
GoI Act 1935 = biggest single source; Constituent Assembly under Cabinet Mission (1946).
Adopted 26 Nov 1949, enforced 26 Jan 1950; took 2 yrs 11 months 18 days.

blocks.text: The Indian Constitution is the **world's lengthiest written constitution**, blending features borrowed from many nations. Its **Preamble** — the 'soul' and 'identity card' — declares India a **Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic** committed to Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.

rows: Longest written constitution; a blend of **rigid & flexible**.
**Parliamentary govt & rule of law (UK), FR & judicial review (USA), DPSP (Ireland), emergency (Germany), Concurrent list (Australia), FD & planning (USSR)**.
**Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic**; Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.
Added **'Socialist, Secular, Integrity'** to the Preamble.
Part of the Constitution (Kesavananda); reflects its **basic structure**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: features & the Preamble

items: **Preamble**: 'We, the People of India… **SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC**… JUSTICE, LIBERTY, EQUALITY, FRATERNITY'. **Socialist, Secular & Integrity** added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)**. In **Berubari (1960)** the SC said the Preamble is not part of the Constitution; reversed in **Kesavananda Bharati (1973)** — it **is** part & aids interpretation (but is non-justiciable).

**Salient features**: **lengthiest written** constitution; **parliamentary** government; **federal with unitary bias** ('quasi-federal'); **blend of rigidity & flexibility**; **integrated & independent judiciary** with judicial review; **single citizenship**; **universal adult franchise**; **secular state**; **fundamental rights + duties + DPSP**; **emergency provisions**.

**Nature of federalism**: strong centre — single constitution, single citizenship, All-India Services, integrated judiciary, emergency powers, residuary powers with centre → 'federal in form, unitary in spirit'.

blocks.text: Prelims trap: the words **Socialist, Secular** & **Integrity** were NOT in the original Preamble — added by the **42nd Amendment, 1976**.

items: Borrowings by country (UK-parliamentary, USA-FR, Ireland-DPSP, USSR-FD) is a top MCQ.

blocks.text: **Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12–35)** are the **justiciable guarantees** protecting citizens against state action, enforceable through the **Supreme Court (Art. 32) and High Courts (Art. 226)**. They are the 'Magna Carta' of the Constitution.

rows: **Arts. 14-18** (equality before law, no discrimination, abolition of untouchability & titles).
**Arts. 19-22** (speech, assembly, movement; protection in arrest — Art. 21 life & liberty).
**Art. 32** — Ambedkar's 'heart and soul'; writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Fundamental Rights (Part III, Arts 12-35)

rows: Equality before law; no discrimination; equal opportunity; **abolition of untouchability (17)** & titles (18).

6 freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession); **protection re: conviction (20)**; **life & personal liberty (21) — right to privacy (Puttaswamy 2017), education (21A)**; preventive detention (22).
Ban on trafficking/forced labour; **no child (<14) in hazardous work (24)**.
Freedom of conscience; manage religious affairs.
Ambedkar's 'heart & soul'; writs — **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo-Warranto**.

items: **Right to Property** was a FR (Art 31) — **removed by 44th Amendment (1978)** → now a **legal right (Art 300A)**.
FRs are **justiciable**, mostly against the **State**; can be **suspended in Emergency** (except **Arts 20 & 21** — never).
Six FRs; Art. 32 = 'heart and soul' (Ambedkar); Art. 21 broadened hugely by the judiciary.
Right to Property was removed as an FR by the 44th Amendment (now Art. 300A, legal right).

blocks.text: **Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A)** are the **moral obligations of citizens**, added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)** on the recommendation of the **Swaran Singh Committee**, inspired by the **USSR** Constitution. Originally 10, now **11**.

rows: **Swaran Singh Committee**; inspired by the **USSR** Constitution.
Originally **10**; the **11th** (education of child 6-14) added by the **86th Amendment (2002)**.
Respect the Constitution, flag & anthem; protect environment; promote harmony; safeguard public property.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Art 51A)

items: Added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)** on the **Swaran Singh Committee** recommendation (inspired by the **USSR** constitution); originally **10**, an **11th** (parents to provide education to children 6-14) added by the **86th Amendment (2002)**.

**The 11 duties** include: abide by the Constitution & respect the flag/anthem; cherish freedom-struggle ideals; protect sovereignty & unity; defend the country; promote harmony & renounce practices derogatory to women; preserve composite culture; **protect environment & wildlife**; develop scientific temper; safeguard public property & abjure violence; strive for excellence.
**Non-justiciable** (no legal penalty directly) but the state may enforce via law; the SC uses them to interpret laws (e.g. environment, Vande Mataram cases).
42nd Amendment (1976), Swaran Singh Committee, USSR inspiration; Part IVA / Art 51A.
Now 11 duties (11th added by 86th Amendment 2002); non-justiciable.

blocks.text: **Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV, Articles 36–51)** are **non-justiciable guidelines** directing the state to secure a **welfare state and social-economic justice**. Borrowed from **Ireland**, they are 'fundamental in the governance of the country'.

rows: Equal pay, living wage, right to work, public health (Arts. 38, 39, 41, 43).
Village panchayats (40), cottage industries, prohibition (47), cow protection (48), SC/ST welfare (46).
**Uniform Civil Code (44)**, separation of judiciary from executive (50), environment & wildlife (48A), international peace (51).
**FR vs DPSP** — resolved via harmony (Minerva Mills: balance is basic structure).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: DPSP (Part IV, Arts 36-51)

items: **Nature**: non-justiciable ideals for the state (from the **Irish** constitution); aim = a **welfare state / economic & social democracy**.

**Classification**: **Socialist** (Arts 38, 39 — equal pay, wealth distribution; 41 work/education; 43 living wage; 47 nutrition/public health), **Gandhian** (40 **Panchayats**, 43 cottage industries, 46 SC/ST/weaker sections, 47 prohibition, 48 cow protection), **Liberal-Intellectual** (44 **Uniform Civil Code**, 45 early-childhood care, 48A environment, 49 monuments, 50 **separation of judiciary from executive**, 51 international peace).
**Amendments added**: 39A (free legal aid), 43A (workers' participation), 48A (environment) — by 42nd Amendment.
**FR vs DPSP conflict**: **Champakam Dorairajan (1951)** → FRs prevail; **Minerva Mills (1980)** → **balance & harmony** between FR & DPSP is part of the **Basic Structure**.
DPSP = Part IV, borrowed from Ireland, non-justiciable; classified socialistic/Gandhian/liberal.
UCC (Art 44), Panchayats (40), environment (48A) are frequently asked.
